title: Helpers you can see in a Claude Code session
lead: When the assistant sends helpers off to work in parallel, the app has always shown a chip at the bottom of the window counting them — but only in sessions running on the app's own engine. In a Claude Code session the same chip never appeared, even though the app was already following every helper's work. Both steps use the same conversation: three helpers, two still working, one finished. Two Yes/No steps.

steps.path: Any Claude Code conversation where the assistant sends helpers out
steps.headline: The bar now counts helpers in a Claude Code session too, in the words Claude Code uses for them.
steps.changed: A chip appears at the bottom saying how many helpers are working — "2 subagents" — and switches to "3 finished" once they all come back. It sits in the same spot, and looks the same, as the chip a session on the app's own engine already gets. The only difference is the word: the app's own helpers are called specialists, Claude Code's are called subagents, because that is what Claude Code calls them everywhere else.
steps.notice: A conversation with no helpers still shows nothing at all — the chip only appears once there is something to count. Clicking it opens the list in the next step.
steps.risk: One more chip on an already busy bar. It is not something you can switch off from the Customize menu, the same as the specialists chip today.

steps.headline: Clicking the chip lists every helper, grouped by whether it is still working.
steps.changed: Today the only place these three helpers exist is one collapsed row in the conversation, which scrolls away as you keep talking. The list gives each one a card: what it was asked to do, which kind of helper it is, how long it has been going, and — folded shut — its briefing, everything it has done so far, and its answer when it lands.
steps.notice: The cards are the same ones the conversation shows, so nothing here can disagree with what you already see in chat. Clicking a helper's name jumps to it in the conversation.
steps.risk: Two things the app's own helpers get are missing here: no Stop button, and no way to tell which helper a permission question came from — Claude Code reports neither.
